# CC_2025 as a cautionary tale {#sec-app-cc .appendix}

```{r}
#| label: cc-app-setup
#| include: false

# cc_2025 is shipped in FULL in data/sample/ (small enough), so this is the
# complete dataset at true class balance, not a fraud-overrepresented sample
# (see data/sample/README.md). This file renders after 4_data.qmd in
# thesis.qmd, so arrow is already loaded, but load it again here (guarded)
# so the appendix also works standalone.
if (!requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  local({
    lp <- .libPaths()
    .libPaths(c(lp, "~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5"))
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(arrow))
    .libPaths(lp)
  })
}

cc_2025 <- arrow::read_parquet("data/sample/cc_2025.parquet")
names(cc_2025) <- tolower(names(cc_2025))
```

- the labels seem to be statistically independent on every single feature.

```{r}
#| label: fig-app-cc-season
#| fig-cap: "Absolutely no seasonal variation on the data."
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| warning: false
#| message: false

cc_2025 |>
  summarise(n = n(), n_fraud = sum(fraud_flag), .by = country) |>
  mutate(fraud_rate = n_fraud / n) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = fraud_rate, x = country)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Country", y = "Fraud rate")

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-app-cc-season
#| fig-cap: "Absolutely no intra-day variation on the data. This means in the night as many transactions and as prevalent to get frauded as it is in the high periods."
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| warning: false
#| message: false


cc_2025 |> 
    mutate(
        hour = lubridate::hour(transaction_date)
    ) |> 
    summarise(
        n = n(),
        fraud_rate = sum(fraud_flag)/n,
        .by = c(hour, transaction_type)
    ) |> 
        ggplot()+
        geom_col(aes(hour, n, fill = transaction_type), alpha= 0.75)+
        geom_line(aes(hour, fraud_rate*1e+6, colour = transaction_type)) #TODO: set the second axis to


```

- the labels seem to be statistically independent on every single feature.

```{r}
#| label: fig-app-cc-country
#| fig-cap: "Per country fraud rates are    all exactly same."
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| warning: false
#| message: false
cc_2025 |>
  summarise(n = n(), n_fraud = sum(fraud_flag), .by = transaction_type) |>
  mutate(fraud_rate = n_fraud / n) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = fraud_rate, x = transaction_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Transaction type", y = "Fraud rate")
```


```{r}
#| label: tbl-in
# exact full-data counts (cc_2025 is shipped whole in data/sample/)
cc_2025 |>
    summarise(
        n = n(),
        .by = c(device_type, is_chip, is_pin_used)
        ) |> 
    arrange(device_type, is_chip, is_pin_used) |> 
    mutate(
        share = n / sum(n),.by = device_type,
        share = glue::glue("{round(share * 100, 1)} %")
        )
```
